passages.title: 이사회 의장 교체 인수인계 메일
passages.passage:
From: Outgoing Chair, Board of Directors
To: Incoming Chair
Subject: What the Handover Documents Won't Tell You

Dear Vivian,

The formal handover binder reaches you Thursday — governance calendars, committee charters, evaluation histories. This letter covers what binders cannot: the load-bearing informal structures you inherit.

Three observations from six years in the seat. First, the CEO processes challenge best in private, before meetings — positions questioned publicly for the first time harden instantly. I brief her on contentious agenda items 48 hours ahead, not to soften the challenge but to make it usable; the practice looks like coziness and functions as rigor. Judge it after you have tried both sequences.

Second, our two newest directors defer visibly to the founders' bloc in open session, then raise sharp concerns privately afterward. The deference is a habit, not a lack of substance — I have taken to calling on them early in discussions, before the founders speak, and the dynamic improves measurably. The practice needs continuing until it becomes unnecessary.

Third, and most delicately: our audit chair is superb and eighteen months from mandatory rotation, and no current committee member can replace him. The recruitment that solves this needs to begin now, though he will read any early search as a vote of no confidence. Sequence it as committee-wide succession planning — which it also genuinely is — and his cooperation will be complete.

None of this constrains you; boards remake themselves around new chairs, as they should. But inherited machinery deserves a manual, and outgoing chairs are the only ones who can write it.

With confidence in the handover,
Gerald

questions.q: Why does Gerald brief the CEO before meetings?
choices: Positions challenged publicly first harden instantly
questions.exKo: 공개 석상에서 처음 반박당한 입장은 즉시 굳어지므로 사전 브리핑이 실효적 견제가 됩니다.

questions.q: How does he counteract the new directors' deference?
choices: Calling on them before the founders speak
questions.exKo: 창업자 그룹 발언 전에 신임 이사들에게 먼저 발언권을 줍니다.

questions.q: Why frame the audit recruitment as committee-wide planning?
choices: The chair would read a targeted search as no confidence
questions.exKo: 조기 후임 물색을 불신임으로 받아들일 수 있어 전체 승계 계획으로 포장해야 협조를 얻습니다.

passages.title: 핵심 부품 이중화 투자 승인 요청 메일
passages.passage:
From: VP Supply Chain
To: CEO, CFO
Subject: Dual-Sourcing the Gearbox — The Insurance We Keep Declining

Dear both,

For the third consecutive year, the budget draft strikes the gearbox dual-sourcing line, and for the third year I am appealing — this time with the numbers our luck has so far spared us from generating.

The exposure: every unit we ship contains a precision gearbox from Halberg GmbH, sole-sourced since 2019. Halberg is excellent — that is precisely the trap. Excellence produced complacency, and complacency has now produced concentration: they supply 70 percent of our segment industry-wide, their order book runs 11 months, and their ownership is in its third year of succession limbo that their own executives describe, privately, as unresolved.

Qualifying Renkata as second source costs 2.8 million over 18 months — tooling, validation, and the engineering hours the budget keeps reallocating. The declined insurance premium, annualized: roughly 1.9 million. Against it: a Halberg disruption of ninety days — strike, sale, fire, choose your scenario — idles our line at 11 million monthly contribution margin, and the recovery queue behind their other customers would not favor us: we are 8 percent of their volume; two competitors are each above 20.

I am not predicting a Halberg failure. I am pricing our inability to survive one. Insurance is always overpriced until the year it is priceless — and the qualification clock cannot be started retroactively.

Requesting 30 minutes at Thursday's session, before the budget locks.

Andrea Voss

questions.q: What is 'precisely the trap' in the email's argument?
choices: The supplier's excellence bred complacent concentration
questions.exKo: 공급사가 훌륭했기 때문에 안심했고, 그 안심이 위험한 집중을 낳았습니다.

questions.q: Why would recovery after a disruption disadvantage the company?
choices: Larger customers would be prioritized in the recovery queue
questions.exKo: 자사는 물량의 8%에 불과해 20%대 경쟁사들에 복구 우선순위가 밀립니다.

questions.q: How does Ms. Voss frame the request?
choices: As pricing survival, not predicting failure
questions.exKo: 공급사 실패 예측이 아니라 실패 시 생존 불능 상태의 가격을 계산한 것입니다.

passages.title: 사고 대응 무비난 사후분석 도입 공지
passages.passage:
BLAMELESS POST-INCIDENT REVIEW — POLICY AND ITS LIMITS

Following the November outage review — which produced two resignations and no systemic fixes — the company adopts blameless post-incident review as standard, with the honesty to state where blamelessness ends.

The premise, borrowed from aviation and medicine: systems that punish error reporting receive fewer reports, not fewer errors. Our own data concurs — near-miss reports doubled at the plant that piloted blameless review, and the fixes those reports generated prevented at least one incident our insurers would have found expensive.

Mechanics: reviews convene within five days, focus on reconstructing conditions rather than assigning fault, and publish findings internally with actions and owners. The facilitating question is 'what made this action seem reasonable at the time?' — because operators do not choose errors; they choose actions whose error becomes visible only afterward, and the conditions that made the wrong action look right are the system's to fix.

The limits, stated plainly because pretending they do not exist would poison the premise: blamelessness covers honest error under normal pressure. It does not cover concealment after the fact, deliberate policy violation for convenience, or arriving impaired — categories that route to standard disciplinary process, unchanged. The distinction in one sentence: we do not punish being wrong; we punish hiding it.

Facilitator training begins next week; the first quarterly learning digest — anonymized patterns across reviews — publishes in March.

Operations & Safety

questions.q: What did the November review produce?
choices: Two resignations and no systemic fixes
questions.exKo: 책임자 사퇴만 낳고 시스템 개선은 전무했던 것이 제도 도입 계기입니다.

questions.q: What is the facilitating question's purpose?
choices: To find conditions that made wrong actions look right
questions.exKo: 당시엔 합리적으로 보였던 이유, 즉 시스템이 고쳐야 할 조건을 찾기 위해서입니다.

questions.q: What does blamelessness NOT cover?
questions.exKo: 은폐, 고의적 규정 위반, 음주 등은 기존 징계 절차 대상입니다.

passages.title: 관리자 승진 요건 개정 공지
passages.passage:
MANAGEMENT PROMOTION CRITERIA — REVISED, WITH REASONS

Effective next cycle, promotion into people-management roles requires evidence in three areas the previous criteria treated as optional, and the reasons belong in the open.

The diagnosis: exit interviews and engagement data agree that management quality varies more within our company than any other factor we measure — and our promotion pattern explains why. We have promoted our strongest individual contributors into management as a reward, then measured them for two years on everything except management. The predictable result appears in our data as 'manager lottery': identical roles, wildly different retention.

The revised requirements. First, demonstrated development of others before promotion — documented mentoring, onboarding leadership, or skill-building of colleagues — because developing people is the job, and wanting the title is not evidence of wanting the work. Second, a management fundamentals program completed in advance, with a simulation-based assessment — feedback conversations, workload triage, a difficult-news scenario — because we assess engineers by engineering before trusting them with production, and management deserves no lower bar. Third, structured input from those the candidate has actually led — project teams, interns, task forces — weighted for pattern, not anecdote.

Simultaneously, the expert track's compensation parity — announced separately — removes the financial motive to seek management for the wrong reason. Wanting to manage should be a choice toward the work, not away from a ceiling.

Current managers are unaffected structurally but enter the same fundamentals program over 18 months — the bar rises for everyone, in order of stakes.

People & Organization

questions.q: What is the 'manager lottery' in the company's data?
choices: Identical roles showing wildly different retention by manager
questions.exKo: 같은 직무인데 관리자에 따라 이직률이 크게 갈리는 현상입니다.

questions.q: Why is prior development of others required?
choices: Developing people is the actual job being applied for
questions.exKo: 사람을 키우는 것이 관리직의 본질이므로 그 증거를 요구합니다.

questions.q: How does expert-track parity support this change?
choices: It removes the financial motive to manage for the wrong reason
questions.exKo: 보상 상한 때문에 관리직을 택하는 왜곡된 동기를 제거합니다.

passages.title: 데이터센터 폐열 활용 컨설팅 광고
passages.passage:
HEATCYCLE — YOUR EXHAUST IS SOMEONE'S UTILITY BILL

Every megawatt your data center draws leaves as heat — engineered away at cost, into air that a district heating network, a greenhouse operator, or an aquaculture farm two kilometers away is paying to produce deliberately. HeatCycle closes that loop commercially, not just thermally.

Our engagements begin with the matchmaking physics: heat quality mapping — your exhaust temperatures against the demand curves of every plausible offtaker within pipe distance — because a match exists only where temperature, timing, and distance align, and most feasibility studies die on the second variable. Where the physics work, we structure the commerce: offtake agreements with indexed pricing, capacity guarantees calibrated to your actual load patterns, and the regulatory navigation — waste-heat classifications, utility interconnection, municipal permits — that has stranded more projects than any engineering failure.

The economics have crossed a threshold worth knowing: with energy-reuse regulations tightening across major markets, recovered heat has shifted from sustainability gesture to rated revenue stream — our completed projects return 4 to 9 percent on the heat-capture retrofit, before counting the compliance value of the reuse ratios regulators increasingly require.

Operators of facilities above 5 megawatts: the feasibility screen is free and takes two weeks — physics first, so nobody's time is spent on a match that thermodynamics already vetoed. heatcycle.energy/screen.

questions.q: Where do most feasibility studies fail, per the ad?
choices: On timing alignment between heat supply and demand
questions.exKo: 온도·시점·거리 중 두 번째 변수인 수요 시점 불일치에서 대부분 좌초합니다.

questions.q: What has shifted recovered heat's status?
choices: Tightening energy-reuse regulations made it a revenue stream
questions.exKo: 에너지 재사용 규제 강화로 지속가능성 제스처에서 수익원으로 바뀌었습니다.

questions.q: Why is the feasibility screen physics-first?
choices: Thermodynamic vetoes should end projects before commercial effort
questions.exKo: 물리적으로 불가능한 조합에 상업 검토 시간을 쓰지 않기 위해서입니다.

passages.title: 지식재산 포트폴리오 정리 서비스 광고
passages.passage:
PATENTPRUNE — YOUR PORTFOLIO IS 40 PERCENT DEADWEIGHT. WE'LL PROVE WHICH 40.

Patent maintenance fees compound silently: a global family kept alive for two decades costs six figures, and portfolios accrete by default because no attorney ever got fired for renewing. Meanwhile the annual renewal decision — thousands of assets, each needing minutes of attention nobody schedules — defaults to 'pay,' and the deadweight grows.

PatentPrune audits portfolios against three questions your renewal process never asks systematically. Does the patent read on anything shipping — yours or infringers'? Claim-mapping against product teardowns and market scans answers with evidence, not recollection. Does it block anyone — would a competitor's design path cross it? Citation forensics and prosecution histories reveal which assets competitors actually engineer around, the truest measure of a claim's teeth. Could someone else monetize what you cannot? Our brokerage arm prices dormant families against active acquisition demand — one client's abandoned-candidate list yielded a sale covering the entire audit fee eightfold.

The deliverable is a decision, not a report: keep, license, sell, or lapse — per family, per jurisdiction, with the fee savings and risk trade-offs quantified. Clients typically cut renewal budgets 30 percent while strengthening enforcement posture, because pruning is how the load-bearing assets become visible.

Portfolios above 500 families: pilot audits on your most doubtful technology cluster at fixed fee. patentprune.ip/pilot.

questions.q: Why do portfolios accrete deadweight?
choices: Renewal defaults to 'pay' since nobody is fired for renewing
questions.exKo: 갱신 거절에는 책임이 따르지만 갱신에는 없어 기본값이 '납부'가 되기 때문입니다.

questions.q: What is called the truest measure of a claim's teeth?
questions.exKo: 경쟁사가 실제로 회피 설계하는 특허가 진짜 힘 있는 특허입니다.

questions.q: What form does the deliverable take?
choices: Per-family decisions: keep, license, sell, or lapse
questions.exKo: 보고서가 아니라 패밀리·국가별 유지/라이선스/매각/포기 결정입니다.

passages.title: 기업 간 데이터 협동조합 확산 기사
passages.passage:
DATA ECONOMY — Competitors are pooling data they once guarded, and the emerging structures — data cooperatives with governance borrowed from agricultural collectives — suggest the practice is maturing from experiment to institution.

The logic is scale no single firm achieves: predictive maintenance models trained on one airline's engine data plateau; trained across nine carriers' pooled histories, failure prediction windows extended enough that two participants restructured their spare-parts networks around the improvement. Similar cooperatives now operate in commercial insurance claims, container logistics, and pharmaceutical cold-chain monitoring — domains where rare events matter most and no participant sees enough of them alone.

The governance innovations are the story's substance. Contribution and extraction are metered: members draw model benefits proportional to data supplied, audited by the cooperative's neutral operator, ending the free-rider dynamic that killed earlier voluntary consortia. Competitive insulation is structural — models output predictions, never raw records, and queries that could reverse-engineer a member's operations are blocked by design, with the blocklist itself governed by member vote. And exit rights are priced honestly: departing members withdraw their data's future contribution but not the trained models' accumulated learning — 'you can leave the choir,' one cooperative director notes, 'but you cannot unsing.'

Regulators, initially wary of coordination risks, have granted two cooperatives formal comfort letters after reviewing their insulation architecture — signals the model's compliance perimeter is becoming legible. Analysts expect the structure to spread wherever rare-event prediction meets fragmented data ownership: 'which,' one observes, 'describes half the industrial economy.'

questions.q: Why do firms pool data despite competing?
choices: Rare-event prediction needs scale no single firm has
questions.exKo: 희귀 사건 예측에는 개별 기업이 확보 못 할 데이터 규모가 필요하기 때문입니다.

questions.q: How is the free-rider problem solved?
choices: Benefits are metered proportional to audited contribution
questions.exKo: 중립 운영자가 감사하는 기여-혜택 비례 구조로 무임승차를 막습니다.

questions.q: What does 'you cannot unsing' describe?
choices: Departing members cannot remove their data's trained-in learning
questions.exKo: 탈퇴해도 이미 모델에 학습된 기여분은 회수할 수 없다는 뜻입니다.

passages.title: 경력 공백 채용 시장 재평가 기사
passages.passage:
LABOR MARKETS — The resume gap, long treated by screening software as a defect requiring explanation, is being repriced by employers who examined their own outcome data — and found the penalty they were applying had no empirical basis.

A consortium of 14 large employers, pooling anonymized hiring and performance records, found that candidates hired after career breaks of one to four years matched their continuous-career peers on every performance measure within 18 months — and exceeded them measurably on two: retention and, in management roles, team engagement scores. The report's authors advance an unsentimental hypothesis: surviving screening prejudice selects for determination, and career breaks — caregiving, health, retraining — frequently build precisely the triage and resilience capabilities management roles consume.

Practice is following evidence. Six consortium members removed gap-flagging from their screening software entirely; several rewrote application forms to ask for 'relevant experience' rather than 'continuous history.' Returnship programs — structured re-entry cohorts with refresher training — report offer-acceptance rates above 90 percent and cost-per-hire below graduate recruiting, prompting one bank to triple its cohort.

The repricing has a competitive edge: firms retaining gap penalties now fish in a pool their rivals have widened. 'Screening rules encode the labor market of the decade they were written,' the report concludes. 'The firms that audit their encodings first hire from everyone else's blind spot.'

questions.q: What did the consortium's data show about career-break hires?
choices: They matched peers and exceeded them on retention and engagement
questions.exKo: 18개월 내 전 지표 동등, 유지율·팀 몰입도는 오히려 우수했습니다.

questions.q: What hypothesis explains the outperformance?
choices: Screening prejudice selects for determination, and breaks build management skills
questions.exKo: 편견을 뚫은 의지와 공백기에 쌓인 위기 대처 역량이 원인이라는 가설입니다.

questions.q: What competitive point does the report close on?
choices: Firms auditing outdated screening rules hire from rivals' blind spots
questions.exKo: 낡은 스크리닝 규칙을 먼저 손보는 회사가 남들의 사각지대에서 인재를 얻습니다.

passages.title: 글로벌 가격 인상 순서 설계 문자
passages.passage:
Linh Tran (9:05 A.M.)
Pricing committee approved the 7 percent increase. Now the harder question — rollout sequence across 12 markets. Big bang or waves?

Erik Molnar (9:11 A.M.)
Waves, and the sequence is strategy. Start with the two markets where our net promoter scores are highest and competitors just raised — the increase lands softest there, and we learn our churn elasticity from friendly territory.

Linh Tran (9:13 A.M.)
And the learning transfers how?

Erik Molnar (9:16 A.M.)
Wave one gives us four weeks of actuals — churn by segment, downgrade rates, win-back costs. Wave two's messaging gets tuned on that: if annual-plan users churn least, wave two leads with the annual lock-in offer. By wave three we're operating on evidence while competitors guess at our results.

Linh Tran (9:18 A.M.)
Risk: wave-one customers hear wave-three markets got two extra months at old prices. Cross-border customers especially.

Erik Molnar (9:21 A.M.)
Handled two ways. Multi-market accounts get synchronized dates regardless of wave — one contract, one date. And the wave gap compresses to six weeks total; resentment needs months to organize, and the differential is smaller than our standard regional price variance anyway.

Linh Tran (9:23 A.M.)
Grandfathering?

Erik Molnar (9:25 A.M.)
Twelve months for anyone who commits annual before their market's date — converts the fence-sitters, rewards loyalty, and every conversion is churn insurance at the exact moment churn risk peaks. The offer costs us the increase's first year on maybe 15 percent of the base, and buys the retention story the increase needs.

Linh Tran (9:26 A.M.)
Modeling all three waves by Friday. Send the market rankings with the NPS-competitor matrix?

Erik Molnar (9:27 A.M.)
Within the hour.

questions.q: Why do the friendliest markets go first?
choices: To learn churn elasticity where the increase lands softest
questions.exKo: 우호적 시장에서 이탈 탄력성 실측치를 안전하게 확보하기 위해서입니다.

questions.q: How are cross-border accounts handled?
questions.exKo: 복수 시장 계정은 웨이브와 무관하게 단일 날짜로 통일합니다.

questions.q: What does the grandfathering offer buy?
choices: Churn insurance exactly when churn risk peaks
questions.exKo: 이탈 위험이 최고조인 시점에 연간 약정 전환으로 잔류를 확보합니다.

passages.title: 연구소 스핀오프 지분 구조 협상 문자
passages.passage:
Prof. Dana Iversen (2:40 P.M.)
The university's proposed terms for our spinoff came back: 25 percent equity plus a 3 percent royalty on the licensed patents. Your reaction before I respond?

Martin Vogel (2:46 P.M.)
Both levers at those levels kills the company politely. Investors model it instantly: 25 percent non-dilutable-in-practice university equity plus a perpetual revenue royalty reads as a cap table with a tax on it. Our seed conversations will die at term-sheet stage.

Prof. Dana Iversen (2:48 P.M.)
The tech transfer office says both are 'standard.'

Martin Vogel (2:51 P.M.)
'Standard' at institutions whose spinoffs mostly stay small. The benchmark that matters: the three universities in our field whose spinoffs actually raised Series B rounds all converged on one lever, not two — either equity around 10 percent that dilutes normally, or royalties, never both stacked. I'll send the comparison table; it's public data.

Prof. Dana Iversen (2:53 P.M.)
Which lever should we argue for?

Martin Vogel (2:56 P.M.)
Equity, 10 percent, standard dilution. Royalties poison hardware startups specifically — our margins in years one to three will be thin, and a revenue royalty taxes us precisely when we can least pay it. Equity aligns the university with our eventual value instead of our early struggle. And offer them the sweetener that costs us nothing: a board observer seat and first-look rights on our future patent filings. They value pipeline visibility more than the royalty spreadsheet suggests.

Prof. Dana Iversen (2:58 P.M.)
And if they hold firm on both levers?

Martin Vogel (3:01 P.M.)
Then we ask one question: 'has a spinoff on these terms ever raised institutional capital in our sector?' — and request they name it. Negotiations anchored to precedent need precedents. If the answer is silence, the terms move; if they name one, I genuinely want to study it.

Prof. Dana Iversen (3:02 P.M.)
Drafting the response tonight with the comparison table attached. Send it over.

Martin Vogel (3:03 P.M.)
Sending now, with the dilution model for both scenarios.

questions.q: Why do the proposed terms threaten the spinoff?
choices: Stacked equity and royalties deter institutional investors
questions.exKo: 25% 지분과 3% 로열티의 중첩은 투자자에게 '세금 붙은 캡테이블'로 읽힙니다.

questions.q: Why is a royalty worse than equity for this startup?
choices: It taxes thin early hardware margins exactly when cash is scarce
questions.exKo: 초기 박한 마진에 매출 로열티가 얹히면 가장 못 견딜 시기에 부담이 커집니다.

questions.q: What is the fallback question's purpose?
choices: Forcing the office to produce a precedent or move the terms
questions.exKo: '이 조건으로 투자 유치한 사례를 대보라'는 요구로 근거 없는 표준 주장을 무너뜨립니다.
